entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 11.01.2019 passed by the II Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT, Raichur, in MVC No.433 of 2017.

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT, Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. One Ramu @
Ramanna

met with an accident on 24.05.2017, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Innova Car bearing No.MH-43/X-7950 and sustained multiple grievous injuries and succumbed to the same during treatment.

Therefore, his wife, children and mother filed a claim petition before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.25,50,000/- with interest at 12% p.a.
4.

The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted total compensation of Rs.15,82,000/- with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed respondent No.2-Insurance Company to deposit the same.

5. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the claimants have preferred this appeal, in which it is NC: 2025:KHC-K:6625 HC-KAR contended that, the deceased was working as mason and earning Rs.15,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has wrongly taken his income at Rs.8,000/- per month and lesser amount is granted under other conventional heads.
Therefore, requested for enhancement of the compensation.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides.
7.
Thought the claimants stated that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, they have not filed any income proof.
Hence, as he met with an accident in the year 2017, as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, his notional income is to be taken at Rs.10,250/- per month.

As per the dictum of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi1, considering the age of the deceased, 40% of the income has to be added towards future prospects, which is rightly considered by the Tribunal.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deduction of 1/4th towards personal (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2025:KHC-K:6625 HC-KAR expenses of the deceased and the multiplier of 15 considered by the Tribunal are also just and proper.

Thus, the loss of dependency would be :
Rs.10,250 + 40% x 12 x 15 x 3/4 = Rs.19,37,250/-
8.

Further, as per the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the dictum of Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & others2, and United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others3, appellant No.1-wife is entitled for Rs.48,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium, appellant Nos.2 and 3- children are entitled for Rs.48,000/- each towards loss of parental consortium and appellant No.4-mother is entitled for Rs.48,000/- towards loss of filial consortium.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In all, they are entitled for total amount of Rs.1,92,000/- under this head.

They are also entitled for an amount of Rs.30,000/- under the conventional heads i.e., loss of estate and funeral expenses as per the citation in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Shivamma And Ors vs Hanumantha B Naik And Anr on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148320814/
3 Vs. Pranay Sethi.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Shivamma And Ors vs Hanumantha B Naik And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
10. Hence, the compensation is reassessed as under:
Loss of dependency Rs.19,37,250/-
Loss of consortium Rs.1,92,000/-
Conventional heads Rs.30,000/-
Total Rs.21,59,250/-
Less awarded by the Tribunal: Rs.15,82,000/-
Enhanced compensation Rs.5,77,250/-
The Insurance Company has already deposited the amount awarded by the Tribunal.

Thus, the appellants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.5,77,250/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

11. In the result, the following order is passed:
(i) The appeal is allowed in part.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6625 HC-KAR (ii) The appellants/claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.5,77,250/- along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.

However, as per order dated 12.07.2023,
the appellants are not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 662 days in filing the appeal.
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, appellant No.1-wife alone is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
